model.rationale: The post-redistricting fundamentals give Democrats a roughly 25-point structural lean, and Frederick Haynes has outraised Everett Jackson by more than 20-to-1 with outside support on his side. Markets price a Democratic win near certain, so the forecast stays at a Safe D rating with a margin near the district's lean.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unusually strong Republican fundraising surge could narrow the margin, though the seat's underlying lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat after redistricting reshaped the Dallas-area district into strongly Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of about 25 points toward Democrats. Frederick Haynes III enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised over $420,000 and drawn roughly $200,000 in outside support, while Republican Everett Jackson has raised about $17,000 with minimal cash on hand.

No public polling covers the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 96 percent. The seat is rated Safe D, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
